Internal — forwarding BrightMart request. Summary below and attachments included in thread.

Key asks from customer (BrightMart):
- Rev-share: 20% on usage (marketplace carve required).
- SLA: 99.95% with 6-hour P1 response (higher than our standard marketplace 99.9 / standard incident SLA).
- Payment terms: Net 60.
- Onboarding: potential one-time onboarding credit (customer hasn't quantified; see forecast).

Why this matters: BrightMart is an anchor account in retail vertical; they will route 3 major product lines through the marketplace if the private offer is acceptable. Forecast attached shows ~$150k ARR in first 6 months with upside for Q4. They prefer marketplace listing for procurement simplicity and to consolidate billing via AWS.

Request: I need an executive approval to deviate on commissions and SLA for a limited window (6 months) and confirmation from Finance on Net 60 exposure. Proposed middle ground I've sketched: 15% rev-share with a usage tier structure (20% for first 90 days, ratchet down to 12% thereafter), SLA exception limited to the first 12 months contingent on runbook access and monitoring hooks, and Net45 instead of Net60 if Finance will not accept Net60. Also proposing a capped onboarding credit of $10k.

Attachments: BrightMart_PO_Draft_v1.pdf, BrightMart_usage_forecast_Q4.xlsx, redlines_marketing_terms.docx

Aisha — thanks for the summary and the attachments. Quick read and recommendations: 

- Rev-share: 20% is above our escalation threshold for marketplace commissions (>16%). This needs exec approval (Marissa) + an explicit carve showing this is a one-off. If we can get a timeboxed ramp (20% for 90 days -> 15% next 90 days -> 12% thereafter) that reduces lifetime leakage and may be acceptable.

- SLA: 99.95% + 6-hour P1 response materially increases our support exposure and could require a higher run-rate (on-call rotations + pre-emptive monitoring). We should accept only if BrightMart commits to runbook access, incident playbooks, and an on-call paging integration (PagerDuty) with a reimbursement for any premium support hours beyond our standard SLO.

- Net60: Finance risk is non-trivial — recommends Net45 and a cap on outstanding receivables tied to usage cadence. Vivek, finance will need to sign off on Net60 or provide a receivables mitigation plan (e.g., credit insurance, ACH holdback).

- Onboarding credit: Cap at $10k tied to milestones (initial listing + first production ingest).

Actionable ask for Marissa: Exec sign-off to approve sales-side commission exception (timeboxed ramp) and SLA exception (conditional). If approved, I'll produce the MS Word redline to the PO and a short approval memo for the exec signature.

Risks: If we accept 20% flat, long-term comp plans will overpay; if we deny, we risk losing the anchor listing to a competitor. Recommend a timeboxed, tiered rev-share with finance mitigations.

Karthik
Senior Manager, Deal Desk
Redwood Inference
